---
figure: FIG. 2
numerals: [22, 24, 30, 36, 66]
---


View: front interior view of the closed clamp along the pipe axis, near side frame material omitted to reveal the interior as a depiction convention. Details of the jaw carriages are shown in FIG. 5. Patent line drawing, black on white, no shading or color. All line work lies well inside the drawing area, clear of the margins.

Geometry to draw:

- An annular body drawn as concentric outer and inner boundary circles centered in the drawing area, the region inside the inner circle empty, the annular body being divided into an upper half and a lower half by radial breaks at the left and at the right. No pipe is drawn.
- Between the two boundary circles, a narrow band of two concentric arcs set toward the outer boundary, divided at the left and at the right.
- A channel outline of two concentric arcs, one just inboard of the band and one just outboard of it, so the band sits within the channel, the channel being divided at the left and at the right in line with the radial breaks.
- Three slideways through the annular body at roughly equal angular intervals, one at the top, one at the lower left and one at the lower right, clear of both breaks, each drawn as two parallel radial lines between the boundary circles.
- In each slideway a carriage drawn as a radially long rectangle narrower than the slideway, passing through the inner circle, stopping short of the centre of the drawing area, and reaching the band at its outer end.
- On the inner end of each carriage a pad drawn as a small block with a concave inner edge, joined to the carriage at a small circle.
- At the outer end of each carriage a small follower circle lying on the band, and around it a slot drawn as an elongated closed outline through the band, inclined so its long direction is neither purely radial nor purely along the band. The slots share one rotational sense.
- In each slideway a spring drawn as a short zigzag line acting between the carriage and the frame, so that it biases the carriage outward.
- A small rectangular projection standing radially outward on the outer boundary circle at the upper right, radially outboard of the channel.

The slideways, the carriages, the pads, the band, the channel, the followers, the springs and the small rectangular projection are shown schematically.
